spec.name: Accordion
spec.description: A stack of sections whose content expands and collapses under a heading, like an FAQ. Use with AccordionItem.

allowsMultipleExpanded.description: Lets several sections be open at once. Otherwise opening one closes the others.

defaultExpandedKeys.description: Sections open at first, by id, when uncontrolled.

isDisabled.description: Disables every section.

onExpandedChange.description: Called with the ids of the open sections.

children.description: AccordionItem elements.

keyboard: Tab moves between section headings
Enter or Space opens or closes the focused section
requirements: Each heading is a real heading (h3 by default) with a button inside, exposing aria-expanded
The button controls its panel (aria-controls), and the panel is labelled by the button
Collapsed content is removed from the tab order and hidden from screen readers
Expanding respects reduced motion
screenReader: Each section is announced as a heading and a button, collapsed or expanded
Opening a section announces it as expanded; its content follows in reading order
Headings appear in the screen reader's headings list, for quick navigation

use_when: FAQs and long help pages
Settings grouped into sections people rarely need all at once
avoid_when: Content everyone needs: show it
Switching between views of the same thing: use Tabs
anti_patterns: Nesting accordions inside accordions
Putting the only important information in a collapsed section

spec.name: ActionButton
spec.description: One button that handles the permission check, an optional confirmation, the pending state and a result message for an action. It does not fetch data, show toasts, cache or route: you pass the function that does the work.

children.description: Button label. Name the action, such as Delete user.

onAction.description: The work. May be async; its resolved value goes to onSuccess and a throw or rejection goes to onError.

permission.description: What the person may do: allow (default), disabled (shown, focusable, says why) or hidden (renders nothing). Use { state: "disabled", reason } to explain. The server must check again.

confirm.tsType: { title: string; description?: string; confirmLabel?: string; cancelLabel?: string; confirmText?: string }
confirm.description: Ask first. Opens an alert dialog (danger tone when the variant is danger); the confirm button runs onAction. confirmText makes the person type a word before it works.

variant.description: Visual emphasis, same as Button.

icon.description: Icon shown before the label. Decorative, so the label must say what the button does.

successMessage.description: Announced politely to screen readers when the action succeeds. Show your own toast in onSuccess if you also want it on screen.

errorMessage.description: Announced politely to screen readers when the action fails.

onSuccess.description: Called with the resolved value when the action succeeds.

onError.description: Called with the error when the action throws or rejects.

onStateChange.description: Called when the state moves between idle, pending, success and error.

keyboard: Enter activates
Space activates
With confirm, Enter or Space opens the dialog; Esc cancels it
requirements: A disabled action with a reason stays focusable (aria-disabled) and its reason is linked with aria-describedby and a tooltip
A disabled action with no reason is a normal disabled button
A hidden action renders nothing
While pending a second press is ignored and the button is marked busy
The result message is announced through a polite status region, not a focus move
screenReader: Announced as a button with its label
Disabled with a reason: announced as dimmed, then the reason is read as its description
Pending: announced as unavailable and busy
Success or failure: the message is spoken politely after the action settles

use_when: A button that calls your API or mutation and needs permission, confirmation, pending and a result
Delete, archive, send and approve actions in tables and forms
avoid_when: Plain navigation: use a link
Submitting a Form: use the form's submit button
Reading or caching data: that stays with your data layer
anti_patterns: Relying on the disabled state as security: the backend must check again
Confirming routine, reversible actions
Hiding the reason when an action is disabled

focusApproval.description: Move focus to an approval box when one appears.

keyboard: Enter / Space on the summary: shows or hides the steps

Progress reads in words ("Working: 1 of 3 steps done"), failures and declines are counted
Each step is a ToolCall, so it announces its own changes

spec.name: AlertDialog
spec.description: Confirmation dialog for destructive or irreversible actions. It cannot be dismissed by clicking outside, and can ask the user to type a word before the confirm button works. Open it with DialogTrigger.

title.description: Heading, also the dialog's accessible name. Phrase it as the question being asked, such as Delete this user?

description.description: What will happen and whether it can be undone. Wired to the dialog with aria-describedby.

confirmLabel.description: Label of the confirm button. Name the action, such as Delete user.

tone.description: Danger styles the confirm button as destructive and starts focus on the cancel button.

confirmText.description: A word the user must type exactly (such as the resource name) before the confirm button is enabled.

onConfirm.description: Called when the user confirms. If it returns a promise, the confirm button shows a pending state and the dialog cannot be dismissed until it settles. The dialog closes when it resolves and stays open if it rejects.

onCancel.description: Called when the user cancels with the cancel button or Esc.

isOpen.description: Controlled open state, for dialogs opened without a DialogTrigger.

defaultOpen.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled and used without a DialogTrigger.

onOpenChange.description: Called when the dialog opens or closes (without a DialogTrigger).

keyboard: Esc cancels
Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog
Enter in the confirmation field confirms once the word matches
requirements: Focus moves into the dialog on open (to Cancel for the danger tone) and returns to the trigger on close
Clicking outside does not dismiss it
The description is linked with aria-describedby so it is read on open
While a confirm is pending, Esc and Cancel are blocked and the confirm button is marked busy
Content behind the dialog is hidden from assistive technology
screenReader: Opening announces an alert dialog with its title, then reads the description
In the danger tone focus lands on Cancel, so a stray Enter does not destroy anything
With confirmText, the field is labelled with the word to type, and Confirm is announced as dimmed until it matches
While pending the confirm button is announced as busy
Closing announces the button that opened it (focus is back there)

use_when: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action such as deleting a record
Making the user prove intent by typing a resource name
avoid_when: Non-destructive choices: use Dialog
Actions that can be undone: use a toast with Undo
Forms with several fields: use Dialog or Sheet
anti_patterns: Vague buttons like OK or Yes: name the action
Using it for routine confirmations, which trains people to click through
Closing the dialog yourself before an async onConfirm settles

spec.name: Alert
spec.description: An inline message about the state of the page or a task: a tip, a success, a warning or an error. For brief confirmations that disappear, use Toast.

children.description: The message. Say what happened and what to do next.

title.description: Optional bold first line, e.g. 'Payment failed'.

variant.description: Tone and urgency. Warning and danger interrupt a screen reader; info and success wait their turn.

onDismiss.description: When set, a close button appears and calls this. You remove the alert.

dismissLabel.description: Accessible name of the close button.

keyboard: Tab reaches the close button, when there is one
Enter or Space dismisses
requirements: Warning and danger use role=alert (announced at once); info and success use role=status (announced politely)
The tone is also said in words for screen readers (Warning:, Error:), and shown by an icon shape, never color alone
The icon is decorative (aria-hidden)
The close button has an accessible name and a visible focus ring
screenReader: A warning or error is announced as soon as it appears, prefixed with its tone
An info or success message is announced after the current speech finishes
The close button is announced as a button named Dismiss

use_when: A message tied to the page or a form that stays until it is fixed or dismissed
Explaining why something is disabled or failed
avoid_when: A short confirmation after an action: use Toast
A decision that blocks the user: use Dialog
An error on one field: use the field's own error message
anti_patterns: Several alerts stacked on one screen
Danger tone for something that is not an error
Rendering an alert that is already on screen again, which re-announces it

spec.name: ApiKeyList
spec.description: A list of API keys with their name, prefix, creation and last use, and scopes as badges. Create key opens a dialog with a name and scopes, then shows the secret once with a Copy button and a warning; it is never shown again. Revoke needs the key name typed to confirm. Your callbacks do the work. UI permission is not security: the server must check again.

keys.tsType: Array<{ id: string; name: string; prefix: string; scopes: string[]; createdAt: Date | string; lastUsedAt?: Date | string | null }>
keys.description: The keys to list. prefix is the visible start of the key (never the secret). scopes are scope ids.

scopes.tsType: Array<{ id: string; label: string; description?: string }>
scopes.description: The scopes a key can have, shown as checkboxes in the create dialog and as badges (by label) in the list.

title.description: The heading of the list.

headingLevel.description: Heading level of the title, 2 to 6.

state.description: The data state: loading, empty (no keys, with Create key), error (with Try again) or ready. Without it an empty keys list shows the empty state.

onRetry.description: Adds a Try again button to the error state.

onCreate.tsType: (name: string, scopes: string[]) => Promise<{ secret: string }>
onCreate.description: Creates the key on your server and resolves with its secret, which is shown once. A throw keeps the dialog open with an error.

onRevoke.tsType: (key: { id: string; name: string; prefix: string; scopes: string[]; createdAt: Date | string; lastUsedAt?: Date | string | null }) => void | Promise<unknown>
onRevoke.description: Revokes the key after the person typed its name; yours, async.

permissions.description: What the app allows: create and revoke. Hidden renders nothing; disabled keeps the control reachable (aria-disabled) with the reason shown and read, and nothing runs. This only changes what people see: the server must check again.

classNames.description: Extra class names for single parts, so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Keys: root, header, title, createButton, list, item, name, prefix, meta, scopes, scope, revokeButton, dialog, form, secret, copyButton, warning, reason, status.

keyboard: Tab: moves through Create key and each Revoke button
In the create dialog: Tab moves through the name, the scopes, Cancel and Create key; Escape cancels
Revoke opens a confirmation where the key name is typed; Enter confirms once it matches
requirements: Keys are a list; each item names the key, its prefix, when it was created and last used, and its scopes
The create dialog asks for a name and at least one scope; problems go in an error summary linked to the fields
The secret is shown once, with a warning in words, and a Copy button that announces "Copied"
Closing the dialog removes the secret from the page; it cannot be shown again
Revoking needs the key name typed and is announced when done; focus then moves to the heading
A disabled action stays focusable and the reason is its description
screenReader: "API keys, heading level 2"
"Create key, button"; "Create API key, dialog"
"Copy this key now. You will not see it again."
"Key Deploy script revoked"

use_when: Letting people create and revoke the keys they use to call your API
A developer or integrations settings page
avoid_when: Sessions or devices: use a list of sessions with a sign out action
Storing the secret: show it once and keep only a hash on your server
anti_patterns: Treating the permissions prop as protection: UI permission is not security, so the server must check again
Keeping the secret in app state after the dialog closed: it is shown once on purpose
Putting the secret in the keys list: only the prefix belongs there

contract.data: The existing keys (without secrets), the available scopes, an async onCreate that returns the secret and an async onRevoke.

spec.name: AppFooter
spec.description: The footer of an application or marketing page: a line of text, link lists and social links. It stacks on a phone and has the same size and spacing on every page.

text.description: The text on the left, usually the copyright line.

links.description: Footer links: a flat list of { label, href }, or groups of { title, links } for the columns layout.

social.description: Social links, such as icon buttons. Give each one an accessible name.

layout.description: simple is one row; columns lists each group under its heading.

navLabel.description: Name of the footer navigation landmark.

renderLink.description: Draw links as your router's link. Return the link with the given className and children.
renderLink.tsType: (props: { link: import("../app-footer/links").FooterLink; className: string; children: import("react").ReactNode }) => import("react").ReactNode

classNames.description: Extra class names for single parts, so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Keys: root, inner, text, nav, group, groupTitle, list, link, social.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the links, then the social slot
requirements: The footer is the page's contentinfo landmark; use one per page
The links sit in a navigation landmark with its own name ("Footer" by default)
In the columns layout each group has a real heading, so people can jump between groups
Links to other sites that open in a new tab say so to screen readers
screenReader: "Footer, navigation"
"Product, heading level 2", then its links as a list

avoid_when: Page-level actions or pagination: those belong in the page
anti_patterns: Different padding or width on each page: use the footer as it is and restyle it once through classNames
More than one footer on a page

spec.name: AppHeader
spec.description: The top bar of an application: a slot for a sidebar toggle, the breadcrumbs, a search button that opens your command palette, your own actions, a notifications bell with an unread count and the account menu. In a narrow space the search folds to an icon.

leading.description: Content at the very start, such as the button that opens or folds the sidebar. Give it an accessible name.

breadcrumbs.description: Where the person is, usually Breadcrumbs. It takes the free space and shortens before anything else.

onSearch.description: Shows the search button and calls this when it is pressed, e.g. to open a CommandPalette. The shortcut shown on it is a hint only: wire the key yourself.

searchLabel.description: Text and accessible name of the search button.

searchShortcut.description: The shortcut hint on the search button, keys separated by a space. Shown only where there is room. Pass an empty string to hide it.

onNotifications.description: Shows the notifications bell and calls this when it is pressed, e.g. to open a panel.

notificationCount.description: How many notifications are unread. Drawn as a badge (99+ above 99) and read with the button's name. Zero or none draws no badge.

notificationsLabel.description: Accessible name of the bell. The count is added: "Notifications, 3 unread".

actions.description: Your own buttons, before the bell and the account menu.

userMenu.description: The account menu at the end, normally a UserMenu.

permissions.description: What the person may do: { search, notifications } as "allow" (default), "disabled" or "hidden", or { state, reason }. A disabled button stays focusable (aria-disabled) and says why. The server must check again.

label.description: Accessible name of the header landmark.

size.description: default is 56 px high; compact is 44 px with smaller controls.

border.description: Draw a line under the header.

sticky.description: Keep the header at the top while the page scrolls.

classNames.description: Class names for the parts, by slot name, added after the built-in ones. Slots: root, leading, breadcrumbs, search, shortcut, actions, notifications, badge, user-menu.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the leading control, the breadcrumbs, search, your actions, the bell and the account menu, in that order
Enter or Space: presses a button
requirements: The bar is a header landmark with its own name; use one per page and keep the page's main landmark outside it
The search button has a visible name, or an accessible name when it folds to an icon; the shortcut hint is for sighted keyboard users and is hidden from screen readers so the name is not read twice
The bell is named with the unread count ("Notifications, 3 unread"); the badge is drawn as a number, not as color alone
A disabled button stays focusable (aria-disabled) and its reason is read with it
The breadcrumbs keep their own navigation landmark
screenReader: "Application header, banner"
"Search, button"
"Notifications, 3 unread, button"
"Account menu, Ada Lovelace, menu button"

use_when: The bar across the top of an application page, inside or beside a sidebar
You want search, notifications and the account menu in one consistent place on every page
avoid_when: You need the whole frame with the sidebar and the phone menu: use DashboardShell
Navigation across the top of a marketing site: use TopNav
A title and the actions for one page: use PageHeader below the bar
anti_patterns: A second search field in the page next to the search button: one search entry point
A count badge with no number for screen readers: set notificationCount instead of drawing your own dot
More than two or three buttons in the actions slot: move the rest into a menu
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling a button only changes what people see, so the server must check again for every request

contract.data: A notification count and the slots you fill: breadcrumbs, actions and the account menu.
customization: leading, breadcrumbs, actions and userMenu slots

spec.name: ApprovalBox
spec.description: Asks someone to approve or decline something the assistant wants to do. It says what will happen, how risky it is and whether it can be undone, in words as well as color.

summary.description: What is about to happen, in plain words, e.g. "Delete 12 draft invoices".

risk.description: How much could go wrong. High risk uses the danger style and interrupts speech.

reversible.description: Whether the action can be undone. Unset says nothing about it.

approveLabel.description: Text of the approve button. Say the action: "Delete invoices" beats "OK".

isPending.description: True while the approval is being processed: shows a spinner and blocks a second press.

autoFocus.description: Move focus to the box when it appears, so a keyboard user lands on the question.

children.description: Extra detail, e.g. the list of items affected.

keyboard: Tab: moves between Deny and Approve
Enter / Space: presses the focused button
requirements: A named group: its name is the summary, so the question is read first
The box is announced when it appears (assertively for high risk, politely otherwise)
Focus goes to the box, not to a button, so a stray Enter can't approve something
Risk is shown as words ("High risk") and a different icon, not only by color
Deny comes first in the tab order; the approving button names the action
The caller is responsible for what happens to focus after an answer (ToolCall returns it to the tool)
screenReader: On appearing: "Approval needed: Delete 12 draft invoices. High risk. This can't be undone."
Then a group named by the summary, with the buttons Deny and Approve

use_when: The assistant needs permission before something that changes data, spends money or contacts someone
avoid_when: Asking about something trivial and reversible: just do it and offer undo
Collecting several fields: use a Dialog with a form
anti_patterns: Approval buttons labelled just OK and Cancel
Taking focus onto the approve button
Showing risk only with a red color

spec.name: AspectRatio
spec.description: A box that keeps a fixed width to height ratio for what it holds, such as an image, a video or a map. It reserves the space before the content loads, so the page does not jump.

ratio.description: Width divided by height as a number (1.5), a "16/9" string, or a preset: square 1/1, video 16/9, photo 3/2, wide 21/9, portrait 3/4.

rounded.description: Rounds the corners with the control radius.

children.description: The content. Images, video and iframes are stretched to fill the box and cropped to cover it.

keyboard: Not interactive: it adds no tab stops
requirements: The box adds no role or name; the content inside carries its own, such as alt text on an image
Content that is cropped must not lose information that matters: pick a ratio that fits it
screenReader: Transparent to screen readers; only the content inside is announced

use_when: Media whose size is not known before it loads
A grid of tiles that must line up
A video or map embed that should scale with its container
avoid_when: Text content: it can overflow the fixed box
Content that must never be cropped, such as a chart with labels at the edges
anti_patterns: Putting long text inside, which gets clipped
Setting a height on the box, which fights the ratio

spec.name: Attachment
spec.description: A chip or card for a file attached to a message or a prompt: its name, size, a type icon, an upload progress bar or error, and an optional remove button. A preview variant shows a thumbnail for pictures. AttachmentList groups several as a list.

name.description: The file name. It is the accessible name of the chip and of its remove button.

sizeText.description: The size as text, e.g. "2.4 MB". Format it yourself so the language and units match the rest of the page.

mediaType.description: The media type, e.g. "application/pdf". It only picks the icon.

variant.description: chip is a compact row with an icon. preview is a card with a thumbnail above the name.

status.description: ready is a normal file. uploading shows a progress bar. error shows the error message.

progress.description: Upload progress from 0 to 100. Leave it out while uploading for an indeterminate bar.

errorMessage.description: What went wrong, shown when status is error.

thumbnail.description: The picture for the preview variant, usually an img with alt text. Without it the type icon is shown.

href.description: Makes the name a link that opens the file.

onPress.description: Makes the name a button that opens or previews the file. Use href or onPress, not both.

onRemove.description: Shows a remove button. Called when it is pressed.

a11y.role: listitem when inside AttachmentList, otherwise a plain group
keyboard: Tab: moves to the name when it is a link or button, then to the remove button
Enter: opens the file from the name
Enter or Space: removes the file from the remove button
requirements: The remove button is named "Remove <file name>" so several of them are told apart
Uploading shows a progressbar named "Uploading <file name>" with its value; without progress it is indeterminate
An error is shown as text with an icon, announced as an alert, and never by color alone
The type icon is decorative; the name and size are real text
A thumbnail has its own alt text; the card does not repeat it
The progress bar stands still for reduced motion
screenReader: "report.pdf, 2.4 MB" then "Remove report.pdf, button"
"Uploading report.pdf, progress bar, 40"
"Upload failed"

Showing files inside a sent message
Showing upload progress and failures for each file

A table of documents with many columns: use a table
anti_patterns: A remove button for a file in an already sent message
Showing an uploading state with no way to see it fail: always handle the error status
A thumbnail with no alt text

spec.description: Content that sharpens and slides into place when it first appears or when it scrolls into view. It is visible to start with, so it never hides content from anyone.

spec.name: Bubble
spec.description: A chat bubble for plain, short messages. Bubble is the chrome around one message: alignment and colour for who sent it, an avatar, a name and a time, a delivery status with Retry, grouped bubbles that merge their corners, and a footer for actions. It does not render structured replies. Message renders an AI turn from typed parts (markdown, tools, charts, sources) and Chat holds the whole conversation; use Bubble for person-to-person or simple text chats, or put a Response inside a Bubble when you want the bubble look around formatted text.

from.description: user sits at the end edge in the action colour; assistant sits at the start edge on a subtle surface.

position.description: Place in a run of consecutive bubbles from the same sender. Bubbles in a run merge the corners that touch. BubbleGroup sets it for you.

name.description: Who sent it. Shown above single and first bubbles, and used in the accessible name.

avatar.description: An Avatar for the sender. Shown beside single and last bubbles; other bubbles in a run keep the space so text lines up.

timestamp.description: When it was sent. Renders a time element with this value as dateTime.

timestampText.description: The visible text for the time, e.g. "10:42". Without it the time is formatted in the reader's locale and time zone after the page loads (the server HTML leaves it empty, so the server and the browser never disagree).

status.description: sending shows "Sending". failed shows "Not sent" and a Retry button when onRetry is given. sent shows nothing.

onRetry.description: Called when Retry is pressed on a failed bubble.

actions.description: The footer: buttons such as copy or regenerate.

attachments.description: Files attached to the message, usually an AttachmentList. Shown inside the bubble below the text.

children.description: The message content.

keyboard: Tab: moves to Retry and to the buttons in the footer
requirements: Each bubble is an article named by its sender, e.g. "Alex message" or "You message"
The time is a real time element with a machine readable dateTime

Sending is a polite status, not only a dimmed bubble
Alignment uses start and end, so the bubbles mirror in right to left languages
A run of bubbles in BubbleGroup is a labelled group and each bubble keeps its own name
Text meets 4.5:1 on both bubble colours
screenReader: "Alex message, article" then the text and the time
"Not sent" then "Retry, button"
"Sending"

Showing delivery state and retry for each message
Grouping several messages from the same sender

A whole conversation with an input and scrolling: use Chat

spec.name: Carousel
spec.description: A row (or column) of slides that scrolls and snaps, with previous and next buttons and slide dots, for a small set of related items such as featured cards or screenshots. Use CarouselItem for each slide. Built on native scroll snapping, so touch and trackpad swiping work without extra code.

label.description: What the carousel shows, e.g. 'Featured plans'. It is the accessible name of the region.

children.description: CarouselItem elements, one per slide.

orientation.description: Direction slides move in. A vertical carousel needs a height (classNames.viewport, default 18rem).

slidesPerView.description: How many slides are visible at once. Narrow containers show fewer: under 400px one, under 640px at most two.

loop.description: Next on the last slide goes back to the first, and Previous on the first goes to the last. Otherwise the buttons stop at the ends.

showArrows.description: Show the Previous and Next buttons.

showDots.description: Show one 'Go to slide N' button per position.

autoplay.description: Move on by itself. A pause and play button is always shown with it. It stops while the pointer is over the carousel or focus is inside it, and never runs when the visitor prefers reduced motion. At the end it returns to the first slide.

autoplayInterval.description: Milliseconds each slide stays when autoplay is on.

index.description: Controlled index of the first visible slide (0 is the first slide).

defaultIndex.description: Index of the first visible slide at first, when uncontrolled.

onIndexChange.description: Called when the first visible slide changes, whether by a button, a key, a dot, a swipe or autoplay.

messages.description: Your own wording, for translation. goTo, slide and slides use {n}, {from}, {to} and {total} where they apply, e.g. 'Go to slide {n}'.

classNames.description: Extra class names for single parts. Keys: root, viewport, controls, arrow, dots, dot, autoplayButton.

keyboard: Tab moves to the carousel, then through its buttons and the links in the visible slides
Left and Right arrows (Up and Down when vertical) move one slide while the carousel itself has focus
Home and End go to the first and last slide
Enter or Space on Previous, Next, a dot or the pause button does what its name says

Each slide has role=group, aria-roledescription=slide and a name like '2 of 5'
Slides that are fully out of view are inert, so Tab and screen readers skip them
Previous and Next are named buttons; at an end they use aria-disabled so focus is not lost
A change the person made is announced politely as 'Slide 2 of 5'; a change made by autoplay is not
Autoplay is off by default; when on it has a pause and play button, stops on hover and focus, and does not run under prefers-reduced-motion
Scrolling between slides is instant under prefers-reduced-motion
Dots are buttons of at least 24 px with aria-current on the current one
screenReader: The region is announced as 'Featured plans, carousel'
Each slide is announced as 'slide, 2 of 5'
After Next, 'Slide 3 of 5' is announced once; while autoplay runs nothing is announced

Touch-first layouts where swiping is natural

Important announcements: rotating content is easy to miss
Long lists: use a list or table with paging
anti_patterns: Turning on autoplay for content people need to read
Putting the only way to complete a task in a slide that is not shown at first
Slides with very different heights

spec.name: Chart
spec.description: A bar, line, area or donut chart drawn in plain SVG without a chart library. It fits its container, can be explored with a pointer or the arrow keys, and always comes with a written summary and a View as table switch that shows the same numbers.

data.description: The labels along the bottom and one or more named series of values. A donut draws the first series only.

title.description: The name of the figure.

summary.description: A sentence that tells the story of the chart. Defaults to a sentence written from the data.

description.description: A line of muted text under the title. When given it is shown instead of the visible summary, which stays available to assistive technology.

actions.description: Controls placed at the right of the header, for example a SegmentedControl that switches the time range. They wrap under the title on narrow widths.

curve.description: How a line or area joins its points: a smooth curve that never overshoots the data, or straight segments. Ignored for bar and donut.

type.description: Bars, a line, a filled area or a donut.

stacked.description: Add the series up instead of drawing them side by side. Applies to bar and area.

height.description: Height of the drawing in pixels. The width follows the container.

showLegend.description: Name each series (or each donut slice) below the drawing. Hidden for a single series except in a donut.

showGrid.description: Draw grid lines behind bar, line and area charts.

valueFormat.description: Turns a value into text for the axis, the tooltip, the labels and the table. Defaults to compact numbers with the data unit.

onSelect.description: Called when a point is clicked, or when Enter or Space is pressed on the active point.
onSelect.tsType: (point: { index: number; label: string; series: string; value: number }) => void

isLoading.description: Show a placeholder the size of the chart instead of the drawing.

emptyMessage.description: Shown when there is nothing to chart.

keyboard: Tab: moves to the plot, which is one tab stop
ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: move to the previous or next value (ArrowUp / ArrowDown on a donut)
Home / End: jump to the first or last value
Escape: clears the active value
Enter / Space: selects the active value (calls onSelect)
requirements: The drawing is decoration; the title, the written summary and the data table carry the meaning
The plot is a single focusable group named by the title, described by the summary, with a visible focus ring
Moving with the keyboard announces the active value as text, for example "Feb: Revenue $26,500, Cost $12,000"
View as table swaps in the same data as an accessible table (aria-pressed on the switch)
Series differ by marker shape or label as well as color; the legend repeats the same marks
A donut names each slice with its percentage; slices are separated by a gap
Colors come only from the chart color tokens and text stays at 4.5:1
Loading is marked with aria-busy and shows no invented numbers
Empty data shows a message instead of an empty frame
screenReader: Announced as a figure named by the title, then the summary text
"Revenue by month. Use the left and right arrow keys to move between values, group"
Each arrow key press reads the active value, such as "Feb: Revenue $26,500, Cost $12,000"
"View as table, toggle button, not pressed"
The table reads every value under its row and column headers

Letting people point at a value to read it exactly

Exact numbers matter most: show a table
A single number with a trend: use Stat with a Sparkline
anti_patterns: A chart with no summary
Telling series apart by color only
A donut with many slices or with several series (it draws the first series only)
Hard-coding series colors instead of the chart color tokens

spec.description: Picks a color. A button shows the current color and opens a panel with a saturation and brightness area, a hue slider, an optional opacity slider, a hex field and preset swatches. ColorPickerPanel is the same panel inline. Values are hex strings.

label.description: Visible label, also the accessible name of the button.

value.description: Controlled color as a hex string: #rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa when showAlpha is on.

defaultValue.description: Initial color when uncontrolled, in the same format.

onChange.description: Called with the new color as lowercase hex: #rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa when showAlpha is on.

presets.description: Hex colors shown as a row of swatches to pick from.

showAlpha.description: Adds an opacity slider and makes the value #rrggbbaa.

format.description: How the color is written on the button. The value is always hex.

description.description: Help text under the button.

errorMessage.description: Shown under the button when isInvalid is true.

isInvalid.description: Marks the color as wrong and shows errorMessage.

isDisabled.description: Prevents opening the panel and dims the field.

name.description: Submits the value with a form under this name.

keyboard: Enter or Space on the button opens the panel; Esc closes it and returns focus to the button
Tab moves through the area, hue slider, opacity slider, hex field and presets
In the color area (one 2D slider), Left and Right Arrow change saturation and Up and Down Arrow change brightness; Page Up and Page Down change by a larger step
In a slider, arrow keys change the value by one step; Home and End jump to the ends
Arrow keys move between preset swatches; Enter or Space picks one
Typing in the hex field changes the color on Enter or when leaving the field

Accepting a low-contrast color for text without telling the person

spec.name: Combobox
spec.description: Text input that filters a list of options as you type. Supports multi-select tags, async loading and long, virtualized lists.

label.description: Visible label.

description.description: Help text under the field.

errorMessage.description: Shown when the field is invalid.

placeholder.description: Hint shown in the empty input.

selectionMode.description: multiple shows the chosen options as removable tags.

value.description: Controlled selection: one key (or null) in single mode, an array of keys in multiple mode.

allowsCustomValue.description: Lets the user keep text that doesn't match an option (single mode).

menuTrigger.description: What opens the list: typing, focusing, or only the button and arrow keys.

isLoading.description: Shows a spinner in the field, e.g. while an async search runs.

virtualized.description: Renders only visible options. Turn on for lists of more than a few hundred items.

emptyMessage.description: Shown when nothing matches the input.

isDisabled.description: Prevents interaction and dims the field.

isInvalid.description: Marks the field invalid and shows errorMessage.

isRequired.description: Requires a selection for form submission.

onLoadMore.description: Called when the user scrolls near the end of the list, for infinite loading.

keyboard: Typing filters the list
Down arrow opens the list; Up/Down arrows move through options
Enter selects, Esc closes and restores the input
Backspace in an empty input removes the last tag (multiple mode)
requirements: Input is labelled and announces the number of results
Each tag has a remove button named 'Remove <option>'
Loading state is announced
screenReader: On focus: the label, combo box, and collapsed or expanded
Typing announces the number of results or the focused option
Moving through options announces each option and its position; in the 5,000-item list, positions like 4,999 of 5,000
No matches: No results is announced
Async: Loading is announced while results load
Multiple: each tag's button is announced as Remove <option>; removing one with Backspace makes its removal clear

Tagging with several values

Rendering thousands of options without virtualized

spec.name: CommandPalette
spec.description: A search box in a dialog that finds and runs commands, jumps to pages and triggers actions from the keyboard. Opens with Ctrl or Cmd + K. Use CommandGroup and CommandItem for the results.

label.description: Accessible name of the dialog, e.g. "Command palette".

children.description: CommandGroup and CommandItem elements.

onOpenChange.description: Called when it opens or closes.

shortcut.description: Letter that opens it with Ctrl (Windows, Linux) or Cmd (Mac) held. Set null to turn the shortcut off and open it yourself.

onAction.description: Called with the id of any command run, in addition to the command's own onAction.

keyboard: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) opens it, and closes it when open
Typing filters the commands as you type
Up and Down arrows move through the results; Home and End jump to the first and last
Enter runs the highlighted command and closes the palette
Esc closes it and returns focus to where you were
requirements: A modal dialog with an accessible name; focus moves into the search box when it opens and is restored on close
The search box stays focused while arrows move a highlight through the results (an active descendant), so typing never stops working
Groups have visible headings that are also read to screen readers
When nothing matches, the empty message is announced
Shortcut hints on commands are display only, read after the command name
The backdrop blur is decoration; the dialog meets 4.5:1 contrast without it
screenReader: Opening announces the dialog name and the search box
Moving through results announces each command with its group and position
Typing announces the number of results, or that there are none
Running a command closes the dialog and focus returns to the page

use_when: Apps with many actions or pages, where search is faster than menus
Power users who prefer the keyboard
avoid_when: A short list of actions: use Menu
Choosing a value for a form field: use Combobox
The only way to reach important features
anti_patterns: Hiding essential navigation behind it
Commands whose names are not words people would search for
Not telling people the shortcut exists

spec.name: ContextMenu
spec.description: The menu that opens at the pointer on a right click, a long press or the keyboard (Shift+F10 or the Menu key) over an area such as a file row. It never replaces a visible way to do the same thing.

label.description: Accessible name of the menu, e.g. "Actions for report.pdf".

children.description: The area the menu belongs to, such as a row or a card. It becomes focusable.

hint.description: Text read by screen readers when the area is focused. It is not shown on screen.

onAction.description: Called with the id of the item chosen.

selectionMode.description: none for actions; single or multiple makes every item checkable.

selectedKeys.description: Controlled selected items when selectionMode is not none.

onSelectionChange.description: Called when the checked items change.

isDisabled.description: Turns the menu off. The area stays as it is and the browser's own menu returns.

elementType.description: The element the area renders as, so a table row stays a row.

keyboard: Shift+F10 or the Menu key on the focused area opens the menu next to it
Up and Down Arrow move between items, wrapping at the ends; Home and End jump to the first and last
Typing a letter moves to the next item starting with it
Enter or Space chooses the item and closes the menu (in a checkable menu, toggles it)
Esc closes the menu and returns focus to the area

The area is focusable (tabIndex 0) and described by a hint, so keyboard and screen reader users learn the menu is there
Opens on right click, on a touch long press, and from the keyboard
Focus returns to the area when the menu closes
Destructive items say what they do in their text, not only in red
screenReader: Focusing the area reads its content followed by "Press Shift+F10 for actions"
Opening announces a menu named by its label and its first item, with its position
Closing returns to the area

use_when: Shortcuts to actions that already have a visible button or menu, on rows, cards or files
Dense lists where every row cannot carry a row of buttons
avoid_when: The action has no other way to be reached: add a button or a Menu
An action list on a button: use Menu
Text fields: leave the browser's own menu (copy, paste)

Disabling the browser menu over a whole page
Nesting a context menu inside another

spec.name: CustomerTable
spec.description: A ready-to-use customer list: search, filters, sorting, pages, CSV export, loading rows, an empty state, an error with retry, cards on a phone, and totals with a chart above that follow the filters. Give it customers and it works.

customers.description: The customers to show. With serverSide, only the current page.

label.description: Accessible name of the table and the section, e.g. "Customers".

currency.description: ISO currency code for revenue, e.g. "USD" or "EUR".

locale.description: Locale for numbers and dates, e.g. "en-GB". Defaults to en-US while rendering on the server and during hydration, then the visitor's language.

isLoading.description: Show loading rows and skeleton cards, disable the controls, and mark the section busy.

error.description: A message to show instead of the list when loading failed.

onRetry.description: Adds a Try again button to the error message.

insights.description: The totals and chart above the table. "auto" works them out from the customers and follows the filters (not with serverSide); "none" hides them; or pass your own numbers.

serverSide.description: The list lives on a server. The table then shows exactly the customers you pass, and asks for new ones through onQueryChange when the search, a filter, the sort or the page changes.

totalCount.description: With serverSide: how many customers match in all, so the pages and the count are right.

onQueryChange.description: With serverSide or a controlled query: called with the new query (search, status, plan, sort, page, pageSize). With serverSide, typing in the search waits for a short pause first.

query.description: Controlled query. Pass the search, filters, sort and page you keep somewhere else, such as the address bar (see customerQuerySchema), and update it in onQueryChange. Without it the table keeps its own.

defaultQuery.description: Start with a search, filters, a sort or a page already set.

onExport.description: Replaces the built-in CSV download. It gets the customers that match (all pages when the list is in memory). With serverSide the Export button is shown only when you provide this.

onOpenCustomer.description: The older name of onSelect: makes each name a button and calls this with the customer, e.g. to open a details panel. Both are called when both are given.

onSelect.description: Makes each name a button and calls this with the customer, e.g. to open a details panel. The conventional name; fires together with onOpenCustomer.

onSearch.description: Called with the search text whenever the search changes (after the short pause with serverSide). It fires in addition to onQueryChange.

onFilter.description: Called with the chosen statuses and plans whenever a filter changes or the filters are cleared. It fires in addition to onQueryChange.

permissions.description: What the app allows, by action: export (the Export CSV button) and open (opening a customer from a name). Each answer is "allow", "disabled", "hidden", true, false or { state, reason }. Hidden removes Export; disabled keeps it focusable with aria-disabled and the reason in a tooltip and read after the button. A disabled open makes the names plain text. Search and filters are always allowed. This only changes what people see: the server must check again.

classNames.description: Class names for the parts of the block, by slot name, added after the built-in ones so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Slots: root, insights, stat, chart, toolbar, search, filters, export, table, cards, empty, error, footer, pagination.

statusTones.description: Which badge color a status gets. The defaults are active green, trial blue, overdue amber, churned red; anything else is neutral.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the search, the filters, Export, the table (one stop), the names when onOpenCustomer is set, and the page buttons
In the table: arrow keys move between cells; Enter or Space on a column header sorts
In a filter: Enter or Space opens the list, arrow keys choose, Escape closes
Escape in the search box clears it
requirements: A labelled region around everything; the table and the phone cards have their own names
A real table with a row header (the customer), sortable column headers that expose their sort direction, and right-aligned money in tabular numerals
The count of matching customers is a polite status message, so filtering is announced; so is an export ("Exported 24 customers to customers.csv")
Search and filters each have a name (read, not drawn); the status of a customer is always text in a badge, never a color alone
Loading marks the region busy and shows skeletons instead of fake numbers; the controls are disabled while loading
An empty list says why (nothing yet, or nothing matches) and offers Clear filters; an error is an alert with a retry button
Below tablet width the table is replaced by cards (a list); only one of the two is in the accessibility tree at a time
The totals and chart come from the Stat and Chart components, so they are readable, keyboard-reachable and have a table view
CSV export neutralises cells that start with = + - or @ so a spreadsheet can't run them as formulas
screenReader: "Customers, region" then the totals, then "Search customers, search edit text"
After typing: "3 customers" (polite)
The table reads as "Customers, table, 24 rows, 5 columns"; a cell reads its row header, column and value
A sort reads "Monthly revenue, column header, sorted descending"

use_when: An admin or billing screen that lists people or accounts with a plan, a status and revenue
You want search, filters, sorting, paging and export without wiring each one
avoid_when: Tens of thousands of rows you must scroll or edit like a spreadsheet: use DataGrid
A list with different columns: build it from Table, Pagination and the other parts, as this block does
anti_patterns: Loading every customer into the browser when there are many thousands: use serverSide
Showing the totals of one page of a server's list as if they were the totals of all customers
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling Export or opening a customer only changes what people see, so the server must check access again for every request

contract.data: A list of customers, or one page of them when serverSide is on, with a plain status tone map.
customization: the parts it is built from (Table, Pagination, Chart, Select)

description.description: One or two sentences under the title.

actions.description: Buttons for the right of the title, e.g. Export and Add customer.

stats.description: The key numbers shown in a row of cards under the title: label, value, and optionally a trend, a small history and a note.

spec.name: DashboardShell
spec.description: The frame of a dashboard or admin app: a sidebar of navigation that folds down to icons, a top bar with search and actions, an account menu, and the page. On a phone, or in any narrow space, the sidebar becomes a menu that slides in.

navigation.description: The navigation as groups of items. An item may hold one level of sub-items. An item may carry a permission ("allow", "disabled", "hidden" or { state, reason }): hidden items, and groups or parents left with nothing, are not drawn or counted; disabled items stay as focusable, non-navigating entries (aria-disabled) with the reason in a tooltip.

currentId.description: The id of the page you are on. It is marked as the current page (aria-current) and its parent opens.

brand.description: Your logo or product name, at the top of the sidebar and the title of the phone menu.

team.description: The organisation or workspace shown at the top of the sidebar, with its logo and a second line such as the plan. Replaces brand there.

teams.description: Other workspaces to switch to. With two or more the team becomes a menu.

onTeamChange.description: Called with the workspace the person chose.

user.description: The signed-in person: shown at the bottom of the sidebar with an account menu.

header.description: Content for the left of the top bar, such as breadcrumbs or the page title.

actions.description: Controls for the right of the top bar, such as a theme switch or a Create button.

onSearch.description: Shows a search button in the top bar and calls this when it is pressed, e.g. to open a command palette.

searchLabel.description: Text and accessible name of the search button.

label.description: Accessible name of the navigation.

skipLabel.description: Text of the skip link, the first thing a keyboard user can press.

onNavigate.description: Called with the item when one is chosen. Items without an href use this to do their work.

renderLink.description: Draw items as your router's link. Return the link with the given className and children; call onClick when chosen. Without it, items with an href are plain links.
renderLink.tsType: (props: { item: import("../sidebar/nav").NavItem; className: string; children: import("react").ReactNode; isCurrent: boolean; onClick: () => void }) => import("react").ReactNode

sidebarAppearance.description: The look of the sidebar and the page: bordered (a line between them), subtle (a tinted sidebar), floating (the sidebar is a raised card) or inset (a tinted background with the page as a rounded card).

sidebarFooter.description: Content above the account area in the sidebar, such as an upgrade card. It is hidden while the sidebar is folded.

isCollapsed.description: Controlled: whether the sidebar is folded down to icons.

onCollapsedChange.description: Called when the person folds or opens the sidebar. Save it if you want it remembered.

classNames.description: Class names for the parts of the shell, by slot name, added after the built-in ones so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Slots: root, skip-link, sidebar, collapse, nav, group, item, sub-list, account, header, search, actions, main, menu-sheet, team-switcher.

children.description: The page.

keyboard: Tab: the skip link first, then the sidebar (collapse button, items, account menu), the top bar, then the page
Enter or Space: follows a link or presses an item; on an item with sub-items, opens and closes its list
In the account menu: arrow keys move, Enter chooses, Escape closes
In the phone menu: Escape closes it, and focus stays inside until it is closed, then returns to the menu button
requirements: A skip link is the first focusable thing and moves focus to the page (a main landmark that can take focus)
The sidebar is a named navigation landmark; there is one main landmark and one header landmark
The current page is marked with aria-current="page" and also shown by a tinted background, an accent-colored icon and a heavier label, never by color alone
An item with sub-items is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the sub-list is hidden when closed
A badge is read after the label ("Inbox, 3") and drawn as a pill; in the folded sidebar it becomes a dot but is still read

The folded sidebar keeps every item's name for assistive technology and shows it in a tooltip on hover and focus; the collapse button (in the top bar) says what it will do (Collapse sidebar, Expand sidebar) and has aria-expanded

On a phone, or when the shell is in a space narrower than 768 px, the sidebar is replaced by a button that opens the same navigation in a sheet; only one of the two is in the accessibility tree at a time
Sidebar width changes stop for visitors who prefer reduced motion
The account button is named with the person's name; the menu is a real menu
A workspace switcher is a menu button named with the current workspace ("Switch workspace, current: Acme Inc"); with only one workspace it is plain text
screenReader: "Skip to main content, link" is the first thing reached with Tab
"Main navigation, navigation", then each item; the current one reads "Customers, current page"
"Reports, button, collapsed" for an item with sub-items, "expanded" once opened
"Account menu, Ada Lovelace, menu button"

use_when: An admin, billing, analytics or internal tool with several sections
You want the navigation, top bar and page frame without building each
avoid_when: A marketing site or a one-page app: a top navigation bar is enough
Navigation that changes with the page content: build it from Menu and Tabs
anti_patterns: Putting the shell inside another shell
Hiding the only way to a section behind the folded sidebar's tooltip: give every item an icon people can tell apart
More than about 7 top-level items in one group without headings
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling an item only changes what people see, so the server must check access again for every request

contract.data: The navigation as plain data: groups of items, each with an id, label, optional href, icon, badge and sub-items.
customization: the Sidebar it is built on

spec.name: DataGrid
spec.description: A fast, accessible data grid for thousands of rows: sorting, filtering, grouping, editing, copy and paste, export and server-side data. Columns are TanStack Table column definitions.

label.description: Accessible name of the grid, e.g. 'Orders'.

data.description: Rows to show. Keep the array reference stable between renders.

columns.description: TanStack Table column definitions. Give each column an id or accessorKey.

getRowId.description: Stable id per row. Needed for selection to survive sorting and filtering.

height.description: Height of the scrolling area in px.

virtualized.description: Renders only visible rows. Keeps 100k rows fast.

sortable.description: Lets users sort by clicking or pressing Enter on a header. Shift adds a secondary sort.

selectionMode.description: Adds a checkbox column and Space-to-select.

onSelectionChange.description: Called with the selected row ids.

globalFilter.description: Shows only rows where some cell contains this text (case-insensitive).

resizableColumns.description: Drag a header edge, or press Alt+Left/Right on a header, to resize.

pinnedColumns.description: Column ids kept visible on the left while scrolling sideways.

showColumnFilters.description: Adds a filter row under the header. Set meta.filter on a column to 'text', 'select' or false.

pageSize.description: Rows per page. When set, a pager is shown; when not, all rows scroll (virtualized).

onCellEdit.description: Called when the user saves an edit in a column with meta.editable. Update your data to apply it.

onCellsEdit.description: Called once with every cell a paste changes. Prefer it to onCellEdit when you paste: applying a whole paste in one update avoids state updates overwriting each other. When it isn't set, a paste calls onCellEdit once per cell.

rangeSelection.description: Select a block of cells with Shift+arrows, Shift+click or by dragging. Ctrl+C copies it as spreadsheet-ready text; Ctrl+V pastes into editable cells.

apiRef.description: Gives you getCsv(), downloadCsv() and downloadExcel() for the rows that pass the filters. Create it with useRef<DataGridApi>(null).

serverSide.description: Your server does the sorting, filtering and paging. The grid shows the rows you pass (one page), reports what the user asked for through onQueryChange, and uses rowCount for the pager. Needs pageSize. Not combined with groupBy or getSubRows.

rowCount.description: serverSide: total rows on the server across all pages, after the current search and filters.

onQueryChange.description: serverSide: called on mount and whenever the sort, filters, search or page change. Typing in a filter waits queryDelay ms; sorting and paging fire at once. Fetch, then pass the new data, rowCount and isLoading.

queryDelay.description: serverSide: milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke in a filter or search before calling onQueryChange.

fillHandle.description: A small handle on the corner of the selection: drag it to fill the cells it covers, continuing numbers (2, 4 gives 6, 8), text that ends in a number (Item 1 gives Item 2), ISO dates and otherwise repeating the values. Ctrl+D and Ctrl+R fill down and right from the keyboard. Needs rangeSelection and an edit handler (onCellEdit or onCellsEdit); only editable cells are written.

columnMenu.description: Adds a menu to every column header: sort, pin, reset width, hide, and show hidden columns again. Alt+Down, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on a header opens it.

rowReorder.description: Adds a drag handle column. Rows can be dragged, or moved with Alt+Up and Alt+Down. The grid reports the move through onRowReorder; you reorder your data. Off while sorting, filtering, grouping or serverSide is in use, because the rows are no longer in your data's order.

onRowAction.description: Called on Enter or double-click on a row, e.g. to open details.

onFilteredDataChange.description: Called with the rows that match the search and column filters, in display order, whenever they change. Use it for counts and totals.

defaultExpanded.description: Start with every group, tree row and detail panel open.

getSubRows.description: Tree data: returns a row's children. Rows with children get an expand toggle and are indented by depth. Search keeps a parent when a child matches.

renderDetail.description: Master-detail: content shown in a panel under a row when it's expanded.

detailHeight.description: Height of each detail panel in px; the panel scrolls if its content is taller.

spec.name: DataTable
spec.description: The list screen every admin, ERP and SaaS app has: a table of rows with search, filters, sorting, pages, selection with bulk actions, a row menu with confirmed actions, CSV export, loading, empty and error states, and cards on a narrow screen. It never fetches: you pass the rows (or one page of them with serverSide) and handle the actions. Permissions only change what people see and can try; they are not security, so the server must check every action again.

rows.description: The rows to show. With serverSide, only the current page.

columns.description: The columns: { id, header, cell?(row), value?(row), sortable?, align?, hideOnMobile?, width? }. The first column names each row (and is the title of a phone card). value is what sorting, searching and the CSV read; without it the row's field named id is used.

getRowId.description: A stable, unique id for a row, such as its database id. Used for selection, focus after a delete and the open link.

label.description: Accessible name of the table and the section, e.g. "Orders".

state.description: The data state, when your data layer gives you one: loading, empty, error or ready. It wins over isLoading and error. A ready table with no matching rows says nothing matches.

isLoading.description: Show loading rows and skeleton cards, disable the controls, and mark the section busy.

error.description: Something went wrong loading: a message to show instead of the rows (true uses a general one).

onRetry.description: Adds a Try again button to the error state.

emptyTitle.description: Title shown when there are no rows at all. Defaults to "Nothing here yet".

emptyAction.description: A control shown in the empty state when there are no rows at all (not when a search found nothing), such as an Add button.

searchable.description: Add a search box. true looks in every column; or list the column ids to look in.

filters.description: Filters shown as selects in the toolbar and in a sheet on a narrow screen: { id, label, options, match? }. Options are text or { value, label }.

query.description: The search, filters, sort and page, when you keep them yourself (for example in the address). Without it the table keeps them.

defaultQuery.description: Start with a search, filters, a sort or a page already set.

onQueryChange.description: Called with the new query whenever the search, a filter, the sort or the page changes (typing waits for a short pause with serverSide). With serverSide, answer it with new rows.

onSearch.description: Called with the search text whenever it changes.

onFilter.description: Called with the chosen values of every filter whenever a filter changes or the filters are cleared.

serverSide.description: The rows live on a server. The table then shows exactly the rows you pass and asks for new ones through onQueryChange.

totalCount.description: With serverSide: how many rows match in all, so the pages and the count are right.

selectionMode.description: Add checkboxes to pick rows. The header box selects the rows on the page.

selectedKeys.description: Controlled selection: the ids of the selected rows.

onSelectionChange.description: Called with the ids of the selected rows.

bulkActions.description: Actions for the selected rows, shown in a bar while something is selected: { id, label, icon?, variant?, permission?, confirm?, onAction(rows) }. A confirm opens a dialog that also says how many rows are affected. The selection clears when the action succeeds.

rowActions.description: The actions of one row, shown in a More menu at the end of the row and of the card: { id, label, permission?, confirm?, variant?, onAction }. Return an empty list for none. After a delete, focus moves to the next row.

onRowOpen.description: Makes the first cell of each row a button and calls this with the row, e.g. to open a details page or panel. onSelect is called too.

onSelect.description: The conventional name for opening a row: called together with onRowOpen.

rowHref.description: Makes the first cell of each row a link to this address instead of a button (onRowOpen and onSelect are still called).

onExport.description: Replaces the built-in CSV download. It gets the rows that match (all pages when the list is in memory) and the query. With serverSide the Export button is shown only when you give this.

permissions.description: What the app allows, by action: export (Export CSV), select (the checkboxes), bulk (the bulk bar as a whole) and rowActions (the More menu). Each answer is "allow", "disabled", "hidden", true, false or { state, reason }. Hidden removes the control; disabled keeps it focusable with the reason where there is a button, and leaves selection off. Single actions have a permission of their own. This only changes what people see: the server must check again.

classNames.description: Class names for the parts of the block, by slot name, added after the built-in ones so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Slots: root, toolbar, search, filters, count, export, bulk-bar, table, header, row, cell, cards, card, empty, error, footer, pagination.

layout.description: Table or cards. auto shows cards when the block itself is narrower than about 640px (not just the screen).

keyboard: Tab: moves through the search, the filters, Export, the table (one stop), the open buttons, the More buttons and the page buttons
In the table: arrow keys move between cells; Enter or Space on a column header sorts; Space on a row checkbox selects
In the More menu: Enter or Space opens it, arrow keys choose, Enter runs, Escape closes
In a filter: Enter or Space opens the list, arrow keys choose, Escape closes
Escape in the search box clears it
requirements: A labelled region around everything; the table and the phone cards have their own names
A real table with a row header (the first column) and sortable column headers that expose their sort direction
The count of results is a polite status message, so filtering is announced; so is the number selected ("3 selected"), and the result of an action
The bulk bar appears without taking focus; after a delete focus moves to the next row, or to the table, never to the page top
Search, filters and the More button each have a name (the More button names the row)
Loading marks the region busy and shows skeletons; the controls are disabled while loading
An empty list says why (nothing yet, or nothing matches) and offers Clear filters when a search or filter is set; an error says what happened and offers a retry
A disabled action stays focusable and says why, instead of vanishing without a word
Below about 640px the table is replaced by cards (a list); only one of the two is in the accessibility tree at a time
CSV export neutralises cells that start with = + - or @ so a spreadsheet can't run them as formulas
screenReader: "Orders, region" then "Search orders, search edit text"
After typing: "3 results" (polite)
The table reads as "Orders, table, 10 rows, 6 columns"; a cell reads its row header, column and value
A sort reads "Total, column header, sorted descending"
Selecting rows reads "3 selected"

use_when: Any admin, ERP or SaaS list: users, orders, invoices, products
You want search, filters, sorting, paging, selection, bulk and row actions and export without wiring each one
avoid_when: Tens of thousands of rows you must scroll or edit like a spreadsheet: use DataGrid
A short list with no search or paging: use Table
anti_patterns: Loading every row into the browser when there are many thousands: use serverSide
A bulk action that deletes without a confirm
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling an action only changes what people see, so the server must check access again for every request
Keeping the selection after rows were deleted elsewhere: let the selection clear when the action succeeds

contract.data: A list of rows of any shape, described by columns, or one page of them when serverSide is on.
permissions: per bulk action and per row action (permission field)
customization: the parts it is built from (Table, Pagination, Select, Menu, ActionButton, AlertDialog)

spec.name: EventCalendar
spec.description: A month grid that shows events on the days they happen. People move between months, step through days with the arrow keys, pick an event, and add one from a day when the app allows it. The app owns the events and the month. Days with more events than fit show a +N more button that opens the full list for that day. UI permission is not security: the server must check again.

events.tsType: Array<{ id: string; title: string; start: string; end?: string; tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"; allDay?: boolean }>
events.description: The events. start and end are ISO strings (2026-10-12 or 2026-10-12T09:30); the date part places the event, the time part is shown. An event with an end on a later day appears on each day it covers.

month.description: The month shown, as YYYY-MM. Use it with onMonthChange to control the month.

defaultMonth.description: The month shown first when the month is not controlled, as YYYY-MM. Default: the current month.

onMonthChange.description: Called with YYYY-MM when someone moves to another month, so you can load that month's events.

weekStartsOn.description: The first day of the week, 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday.

locale.description: A BCP 47 locale for month, day and time names, e.g. "de-DE". Default: en-US on the server and during hydration, then the browser's.

today.description: The date treated as today, as YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the device's date. Set it for stable screenshots and tests.

maxEventsPerDay.description: How many events a day shows before the rest go behind "+N more".

label.description: Names the grid for screen readers, together with the month.

onEventSelect.tsType: (event: { id: string; title: string; start: string; end?: string; tone?: "neutral" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"; allDay?: boolean }) => void
onEventSelect.description: Called when someone picks an event.

onDateSelect.description: Called with YYYY-MM-DD when someone picks a day (click, Enter or Space).

onCreate.description: Called with YYYY-MM-DD when someone uses a day's add button. The button shows only when this is set and permissions.create allows it.

state.description: loading shows a skeleton grid and marks the calendar busy, empty says there are no events, error says they could not load. ready or no state shows the month.

onRetry.description: Called by the Try again button in the error state.

permissions.description: What the app allows: create. Hidden leaves the add buttons out; disabled keeps them reachable (aria-disabled) with the reason read, and nothing runs. This only changes what people see: the server must check again.

classNames.description: Extra class names for single parts, so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Keys: root, header, title, nav, grid, weekday, day, dayNumber, event, more, addButton, popover.

keyboard: Tab: moves into the grid on one day, then to the controls inside that day
Arrow keys: move between days, across month edges
Home and End: first and last day of the week
Page Up and Page Down: previous and next month
Enter or Space: picks the day
Escape: closes the +N more list
requirements: A grid with column headers for the weekdays and one row per week
Only one day is in the tab order; the arrow keys move it (roving tabindex)
Each day names its full date and how many events it has

spec.name: InviteDialog
spec.description: A dialog for inviting people, in three shapes: typed emails with a role on one compact line each, a search of a directory you pass, or a two-step pick-from-a-list with a role per person. Checks for format, duplicates and people who are already members, an error summary, an optional message and a submit button that says how many invitations it sends. Your onInvite does the work. UI permission is not security: the server must check again.

roles.tsType: Array<{ id: string; label: string; description?: string }>
roles.description: The roles a person can be invited as. The description of a role shows in the open list of the role select.

defaultRole.description: The id of the role each new row starts with. Defaults to the first role.

existingEmails.description: Emails that are already members. Typing one is an error on that row. Compared without case.

defaultInvites.description: Rows the emails variant starts with, for example people to invite again. Without it there is one empty row.

people.tsType: Array<{ id: string; name: string; email: string; avatarUrl?: string }>
people.description: The directory for the search and list variants. In search it is what the search looks in unless onSearch is given; in list it is every person that can be picked.

onSearch.tsType: (query: string) => Array<{ id: string; name: string; email: string; avatarUrl?: string }> | Promise<Array<{ id: string; name: string; email: string; avatarUrl?: string }>>
onSearch.description: Search variant only: looks people up on your server as the person types. Return the matches; the latest query wins. Without it, people is filtered in the browser.

maxVisibleRows.description: Rows shown before the list scrolls inside itself, with a fade at the edge that has more. The dialog never grows past 90% of the screen height.

maxInvites.description: The most people one send can hold. Add another is disabled at the limit and says so.

title.description: The dialog's title, shown as its heading. Default: "Invite people"; the list variant shows "Select users" and then "Give user role".

successMessage.description: The status message announced once the dialog has closed after a send. Default: "3 invitations sent".

onCancel.description: Called when the person cancels: the Cancel button or Escape.

onOpenChange.description: Called with false when the dialog closes after a cancel or a successful send. Needed with isOpen.

isOpen.description: Controlled open state, for a dialog opened without a DialogTrigger.

permissions.description: What the app allows: invite. Hidden renders nothing; disabled keeps the dialog but the submit button stays focusable with aria-disabled and the reason shown and read, and nothing is sent. This only changes what people see: the server must check again.

classNames.description: Extra class names for single parts, so you can restyle one part without editing the file. Keys: dialog, form, list, message, toggle, search, results, counter, actions, cancelButton, submitButton, reason, status.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the rows, Add another, the message switch, Cancel and the submit button; focus stays inside the dialog
Escape: cancels and closes
Enter in an email field: sends
Search variant: Down arrow from the search field moves into the results; Enter adds the person
List variant: Up and Down move between people, Space or Enter picks or drops one, Next goes to the roles step, Prev comes back

After a send that worked the dialog closes and focus returns to the control that opened it

"Send 3 invitations, button"
"3 invitations sent" after the dialog closes

onRetry.description: Adds a Try again button to the error state.

onAdd.description: Starts adding a method from the empty state; yours, async.

onRemove.tsType: (method: { id: string; brand?: string; last4: string; expMonth: number; expYear: number; holder?: string; isDefault?: boolean }) => void | Promise<unknown>
onRemove.description: Removes the method after the person confirmed; yours, async.

onMakeDefault.tsType: (method: { id: string; brand?: string; last4: string; expMonth: number; expYear: number; holder?: string; isDefault?: boolean }) => void | Promise<unknown>
onMakeDefault.description: Makes this the default method; yours, async. The button is not shown on the default method.

spec.description: The avatar button that opens the account menu: the person's name and email at the top, your own entries (settings, billing, help) in groups, a row for the theme, and a Sign out entry that can ask first, shows that it is working, and tells screen readers how it went.

user.description: The signed-in person: name (also the accessible name), email and the picture. Without a picture the initials are shown.
user.tsType: { name: string; email?: string; avatarUrl?: string }

items.description: Entries above Sign out: { id, label, icon?, href?, onSelect?, permission?, variant? }. An entry with an href is a link; without one it is a button that calls onSelect. permission is "allow", "disabled", "hidden" or { state, reason }: hidden entries are not drawn, disabled ones are shown dimmed with the reason beside them.

groups.description: More entries in groups, each with an optional heading. A separator is drawn between groups, and before Sign out.

themeRow.description: A row under the entries for choosing the theme, for example your segmented control. It sits below the menu inside the same popover and is reached with Tab.

onSignOut.description: Adds the Sign out entry and does the work. May be async. While it runs the entry shows it is pending; a throw or rejection is an error. Call your own sign-out API here; the library does not.

confirm.description: Ask before signing out. Opens an alert dialog, for example { title: "Sign out of Loomworks?" }; its confirm button runs onSignOut.
confirm.tsType: { title: string; description?: string; confirmLabel?: string }

signOutLabel.description: Text of the Sign out entry.

signingOutLabel.description: Text of the entry while the sign-out is running.

signedOutMessage.description: Announced politely when the sign-out succeeds. It is spoken from a status region that stays on the page after the menu closes.

errorMessage.description: Announced politely when the sign-out fails.
errorMessage.default: Could not sign out. Try again.

onSignedOut.description: Called after a successful sign-out, with what onSignOut returned. Usually where you go to the sign-in page.

onError.description: Called with the error when onSignOut throws or rejects.

permissions.description: What the person may do: { signOut } as "allow" (default), "disabled" or "hidden", or { state, reason }. The server must check again.

align.description: Which edge of the button the menu lines up with.

showName.description: Show the name and email beside the picture in the button. Use it where there is room, such as a sidebar.

label.description: Start of the button's accessible name. The person's name is added: "Account menu, Ada Lovelace".

classNames.description: Class names for the parts, by slot name, added after the built-in ones. Slots: root, trigger, avatar, name, popover, header, list, item, separator, theme, status.

keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the button: opens the menu
Arrow keys: move between entries; Home and End: first and last
Enter or Space: chooses an entry
Escape: closes the menu and returns focus to the button
Tab (with a theme row): moves from the menu to the controls in the row
requirements: The button is named with the person's name ("Account menu, Ada Lovelace"); the picture is decorative
The menu is a real menu named by the person's name; the entries are menu items or links
Closing the menu returns focus to the button
Sign out: while it runs the entry says so and a second choice is ignored; the result is announced politely from a status region that stays after the menu closes, not by moving focus
With confirm, the alert dialog traps focus, starts on the safe choice, and focus returns to the button when it closes
A disabled entry says why in text beside it, not only in a tooltip
A destructive entry is shown in the danger color and also says what it does in words
